name: Season Beating's

date.source: The show's own eight posts' shared dateline; the line-up post's own header, "ICW SEASON BEATING'S PPV LINE-UP."

matches.how: The bell rang for a time-limit draw before the referee's three-count finished; Reed then powerslammed Young from the top rope after the bell and pinned him unopposed. The broadcast calls it a cheap-shot win, not a formal decision.
matches.note: Irregular finish: officially a time-limit draw, credited on air to Reed.
Billed as Bagwell's last match in the ICW; he signed on as an ICW announcer afterward.

The broadcast announces the International Championship vacated ahead of this match, its winner to be recognized with a new North American belt; Bell, the reigning International/North American champion, retained.

matches.stipulation: ICW Light-Heavyweight Championship (billed as the Cruiserweight title in commentary)
matches.note: The recovered text breaks off mid-match; no result survives.

matches.stipulation: Special Challenge Steel Cage Triangle Match, elimination rules
matches.note: J'ster is eliminated before Dark Vanity pins Shawn Riser.

matches.stipulation: ICW World Tag Team Championship, tournament final
matches.how: pinfall (Ron Tenille pins Eddy Ramos) after Zulu Nation's interference (chair shots to both Damage Incorporated wrestlers)
matches.note: Billed as each team's fourth tournament win; crowns the title's first champions.

Billed on the announced line-up, but no broadcast segment for this match survives among the seven recovered parts; Chris Harrison is seen later in the Royal Rumble instead, so the match may simply have gone unaired in the surviving text rather than being cut in-story.

matches.stipulation: ICW Royal Rumble, billed as a 30-man over-the-top-rope elimination match
matches.note: Only the #1 (Glenn Hudson) and #2 (Todd Newkirk) draws are individually narrated in the surviving text; "Bad Boy" Mark Bagwell runs in against Newkirk late in the match, is tricked into knocking himself out with his own microphone, and is thrown over the top rope himself before Newkirk wins.
Immediately afterward, two unidentified attackers run in and chair-shot both Magus and Newkirk as the broadcast ends; the identity and follow-up (if any) do not survive in the held record.

notes: The fed's only complete surviving card: an announced line-up post plus a seven-part broadcast script (parts I-VII), all dated 17 January 1997 and cross-consistent. Also named on air but not separately structured: "Diamond" Dan Round and Rick Showboat (billed as surprise in-ring returns ahead of the Royal Rumble), a real-name-billed IIWF crossover star crashing the show ahead of the first match (redacted per the privacy rule) who returns during the Royal Rumble alongside a second real-name-billed crossover wrestler (also redacted), and "Iceman" Brian Knight's own feud framing with Todd Newkirk. The Royal Rumble itself is far larger than this pass structures: at least a dozen further named entrants (including a fictional-namesake collision, filed to a workshop file) are read in the surviving text but not minted as characters. President Clark presented the fed's own 1996 "Wrestler of the Year" award to Curt Crane on air (see awards.json); Crane's own acceptance interview recaps his ICW World Title win at the fed's "ICW Blood Bowl" tournament (1996, not separately structured here; escalated as an untabled 1997-corpus series). The card advertises a follow-up PPV, "Clash of the Titans," not attested elsewhere in this corpus.
